utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everybody. Madam Registrar, could you kindly call the case, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Merci. All the accused are here. Defence teams are all here. No exceptions. Prosecution is Mr. McCloskey and Mr. Nicholls. The witness is here too. I take it that there are no preliminaries. Good afternoon to you, Mr. Bircakovic. Welcome and we are going to proceed with your cross-examination. And I hope that you've had enough time to compare the two texts that you are in a position to proceed. I'll revert back to you, Mr. Zivanovic. Are new a position to proceed? Are new a position to proceed now?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Bircakovic.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I have now had the opportunity to compare the texts I received from the Prosecution and the one I showed you yesterday, and I didn't find any significant differences that would affect what I want to ask you. I suppose you too had occasion to see these texts. I don't know how focused you were and how willing you were to read it, because you probably have other concerns. Let me remind you where I left off yesterday. I'd quoted a part of your interview that you gave to the investigators of this Tribunal on the 13th of March, 2002. It was on page 15, if you want to follow. In English, it is 24, and it continues on 25. I will read to you your answer that you gave to the question whether Popovic was at school on the 14th. You said, "I'm not sure about Popovic, whether he was there or not. Yes and no. I know from other people that they were there, I didn't see them. There was a Lieutenant of the military police and two policemen and they were from the corps command. Now, what they were doing there, I'm not aware." And then you on to say, "Vaguely I remember Popovic was there and he wasn't there. I cannot be 100 per cent sure because, look, it was a long time ago. Those were times long past. Sometimes I can't even remember what I was doing earlier today. I know as they say, you know," unquote. Were you able to see that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Is that what you answered then?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: If you look at the same page, last paragraph, you continue your explanation and you say, "I can't tell you about something I didn't see because, look, I cannot say that you were there doing any killing because I didn't see you. That is a major accusation. It's not like car theft. I can't say something if I didn't see it." So do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You see, Mr. Bircakovic, this event is -- was something quite impressive in your life, everybody of your -- in your home time knew about it, talked about it, it must have been the talk of the town for years now. You've heard a lot of things from many people, second-hand, third-hand information, and I'm certain that you've read a lot about it in the newspapers, maybe if you even followed earlier trials concerning Srebrenica. A lot has been reported on television and other media. Now, my question is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Sorry, just two points. I want to point out for the record that what is being said is in the transcript is not verbatim. What we have in the transcript of the interview, of course, because my friend is asking his questions in Serbian which are then being translated into English. I just want to make it clear for the record that what we see there is not exactly verbatim what we have in the English version of the transcript. And the second point I have is that when my friend said,"And you continue your explanation," and then read out a second quote from the paragraph, starting at page 3, line 1, it's not absolutely clear and my objection would be that it's exactly the same topic of whether the witness saw Mr. Popovic at the school, because the question before that, which was not read out was, "You don't want -- I understand you don't want to tell me who was at the killing point but I'll urge you to tell me that." So it's moved on to a different topic, and the way it was presented, it sounded a bit as though it was all following the same question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. I think we need to address both these. I don't think it's of any interest to the witness to follow the debate but I think what you need to clarify in the first place is whether the difference there is between the transcript that we have of Mr. Zivanovic's question and the translation of the interview is a substantial one or if it's just minimal. If it's a substantial one, perhaps you can address the Chamber and explain to us how it is substantially different. Witness, do you understand English?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Can I ask you to remove your headphones while we discuss this, please? Yes. Is there substantial difference between the two versions, the English translation of the interview and the transcript in English of Mr. Zivanovic's quotation?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. The thrust is the same. I just wanted to, as I said, make it clear for the record that what was being read was not necessarily verbatim word for word what we have here because it might turn out to be important later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It has no bearing, no relevance as such on the substance of the question and the elicited answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: The substance and the answer are basically very -- are close.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just wanted to make sure of that, because as you know, we don't have a copy of the statement in either of the two languages. The other -- the second point you raised, again, could you explain it better? Because it's not that I am not understanding but perhaps a more comprehensive explanation is called for.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And perhaps you should have the English version for you while part -- just the parts that are being read out to the witness. I don't think there can be any objection to that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: If it's important to avoid any differences, maybe we could be given a copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's a good idea as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's a good idea and not sometimes. It depends. What's the opinion of the Defence benches, Defence teams on this? Would you agree that we are shown a copy of the English version of the interview, the relevant parts, anyway?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: It's 4D105.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think it's much better and the interpreters can follow better, we can follow better, because otherwise, we can only rely on what you are saying without really understanding the import of --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes. It's just because otherwise, we have that extra layer, and this way Your Honours can see if there is anything that you feel important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's concentrate on the second point you raised rather than on the first because if the difference in substance does not exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes. My second point is as follows, and this is on page 24 of the English transcript. The question from Mr. Manning is was Beara --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Wait, wait, wait, wait, wait.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes, we see the question here,"Was Beara or Popovic at the school," and then the answer which was read back. And if we can now go to the next page, the witness has finished saying,"As for Popovic, I'm not sure," we see at the top of page 25 and if we scroll down, scroll down, please, and then we see, "I also understand that you don't want to tell me who was at the killing points at Orahovac." That's now being asked by Mr. Manning. And the answer is, "I cannot tell you something that I haven't seen. I cannot say that you were there killing people." So we've now moved on to a different topic, and the way the question was read out, it may have been -- I'm not suggesting any bad faith, but it sounded as though this answer and the other part that was read out were both in response to the same question, was Popovic at the school, whereas this one has now moved on to, can you tell me who, if anyone, was at the killing site. So I just wanted to point that out because I think it's important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nicholls. I'm just going through the transcript of what Mr. Zivanovic stated. The only thing is this, and again I would prefer to air this out and discuss it with you while the witness is not able to follow. Yours was a pretty long question, and I'm referring you to page 2, lines 10 basically right through line 22, and you are referring him to the first part of -- that was read out, namely, what is contained on page 24, and this is obviously in relation and exclusively in relation to your client, Popovic. You asked the witness to tell you whether he has seen it and he confirms that he can see it, has seen it, and the transcript of his interview. You ask him whether this is indeed what he told the investigator, and he tells you yes. And then, as if you are still dealing with the same subject matter, namely whether he had seen your client, Popovic, or not, you continue as follows, if you look at the same page, last paragraph, you continue your explanation. This is a completely different explanation that he has embarked upon now in his interview. And you say, "I can't tell you about something I didn't see because, look, I cannot say that you were there doing any killings because I didn't see you. That is a major accusation. It's not like car theft. I can't say anything if I didn't see it." He said this in the context of a specific question that was put to him, namely that the investigator, Mr. Manning, was suggesting to him that he was reluctant to tell him, Mr. Manning, that is, who was at the killing point at Orahovac. But I'll urge you to tell me that. So if you could adjust your question basically and explain it better, put it better to the witness. Mr. Bircakovic. Have you understood me?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course. Your Honour, I would just like to give you a brief clarification. These questions that have to do with the presence of my client and some others --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I suspect possibly, based on the Court's earlier asking the witness to take the headphones off, we might be going there again, if he's going to explain the questions and why it's important. He's going back to the same topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go straight to your question. You don't need to explain to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, we left off at this last page, this last question of mine, when you said, "I can't tell you about something I didn't see." Did you mean that? Did you mean only something that you didn't see on the execution site or did you mean something that you didn't see outside the school in general?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was speaking generally, something that I didn't see.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: In other words, you wouldn't speak about anything that you didn't see that happened outside the school, possibly, if you didn't see it?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, you said -- in fact, during your interview, Mr. Manning came back to that issue once again, and let me quote, that's page 39 of that text in B/C/S that you have in front of you, right at the beginning, and in English it's 62. The investigator, Dean Manning, asks you,"At that moment, were there any other people who were in charge of security, people from the corps, like Popovic?" Answer, your answer: "I'm not 100 per cent sure. It seems to me he was there and he wasn't. I can't say anything. I know that I heard it, I didn't see it, I saw there was some Lieutenant from the corps and two military policemen." After that, another question follows: "What is Popovic's rank?" And you answer: "I think he's Lieutenant Colonel, Colonel." Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Now I will continue where I left off before. I've already said that this event must stand out in your life, it's very well known in the town in which you live, and I'm certain it was the subject of a lot of talk and many stories that you must have heard and listened to; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rarely.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You must have had a lot of opportunity to follow reports on TV, in newspapers?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Will you explain what does it mean, "not much"? Do you mean to say you didn't talk to anybody about it or you spoke to a limited circle of people?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't discuss that subject at all, for the most part.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: When you say you didn't discuss it, you mean you did not talk to anyone about it?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: But you had occasion to hear all sorts of talk from others?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not really.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me explain why I'm asking this. Obviously, in this interview as well, you emphasised that it was very difficult to remember details you may have heard or seen after eight years. I suppose it's even harder after 12 years. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Partly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: We have a major difference here, a discrepancy, between your testimony yesterday and what you said in the interview that I just quoted back at you. You said yesterday you were 99 per cent sure that you had seen Popovic outside the school. You didn't say that in the interview. You said something different. Could you tell me whether perhaps all sorts of talk you heard or media reports you may have followed, something you read or heard may have caused you to confuse these things, to confuse these events, to create in your mind a false image that you had seen something like that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: When you say, "I don't know," is it possible?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Just objecting to the extent that his question misrepresents the testimony. The witness said that there weren't all sorts of media that he followed. I heard he hadn't followed it much, he hadn't talked much, and the question put to the witness is as though the witness said, Yes I've been following this, I've been looking at newspapers, TV, talking about it constantly. That's the way the question is phrased. It's the opposite of what the witness answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. What did you -- what is your comment to that, Mr. Zivanovic? If you look at a previous question of yours, and then we go to page --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't say that he had long conversations or that there was a media following but that there was something -- he said it himself, he said that that was a rare occasion. However, rare those things may be, those conversations and media following, he might have still arrived at the wrong conclusions. This is what I wanted to ask the witness. Is it possible that the conversations, that what he saw and listened to, might have influenced his opinion and his testimony that he provided yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Previously, if you look at page 3, lines 8 to 15, you put the following question to the witness, which was not answered because of Mr. Nicholls's interjecting with his objection. You told the witness, "You see, Mr. Bircakovic, this event is -- was something quite impressive in your life, everybody of your -- in your home town knew about it, talked about it, it must have been the talk of the town for years," whatever that word is, "you've heard a lot of things from many people second-hand, third-hand information and I'm certain that you have read a lot about it in the newspapers, maybe if you even followed earlier trials concerning Srebrenica, a lot has been reported on television and other media." This is the prelude to your question, which never arrived at that point in time. You said, "Now my question is" and you were interrupted. He never agreed with you that he's been interested in second, third-hand information or TV broadcasts of proceedings or newspaper articles. He's never -- he's never answered or reacted to that. And now, if you look to -- at your last question, you say, "Could you tell me whether perhaps all sorts of talks you heard or media reports you may have followed, something you read or heard, may have caused you to confuse these things, to confuse these events, to create in your mind a false image that you had seen something like that." I think you have to take it in steps, one by one. First you need to ask him whether he confirms his statements; and secondly, you may proceed to ask him for an explanation why in your opinion there is a discrepancy, and if he could attribute this discrepancy or some possible confusion in his mind to anything. But I would suggest that you do not suggest to him things that he hasn't accepted as yet. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I have put this question to the witness on page 9. I had repeated it, and then he said that he did follow everything but rarely. This is on page 9, line 14, and it goes on -- in lines 14 to 22, I believe. He said he did follow the reports but not a lot, he did it only rarely. Within that context, I put my question to him because I was of the opinion that even the rare occasions when he followed reports might still have influenced his opinion and his testimony, however rare those occasions might have been.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Rarely was to talk and stories that he may have heard or listened to. As regards reports on TV, newspapers, he told you specifically not much, left it in that vague manner. So just go straight to the point. You're suggesting to him that there is a discrepancy between his two versions. Ask him if --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [In English] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- if he has an explanation for that and whether it could be attributed to third --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I'm going to put my question to you in this sense. The difference between what you said in the interview that I've just quoted to you and what you said yesterday can be ascribed by the lapse of time on the one hand, and on the other hand, by some influences that you might have experienced through conversations or following media reports, reading newspapers and watching TV and so on and so forth. Your answer was, I don't know, and I asked you whether this was possible.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that at the time that it was both possible and impossible. A lot of time did lapse.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Is this your position still today, as you sit here today?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is possible and it is not possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I'd like to ask you something else and draw your attention to another part of your interview. I've noticed another difference relative to the time period when you received an order from Milorad Trbic on the 14th of July to take your car and go somewhere from the barracks. You said that that was between 7.00 and 8.00?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between half past 7.00 and 8.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. It might have been that. In your interview, you said that this was between 9.00 and 10.00. I'm very interested in that particular time, and if you want to consult your statement, this is on page 23 of your interview and in the English version, it is on page 37. Did you find it?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, which of the two versions would you say is more correct, if you can remember at all, because, again, it was a long time ago. Would you accept the version provided to the investigators earlier on or would you accept the version that you provided us with yesterday, the new version of that time?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in the morning. I couldn't exactly follow the time. It might have been an hour earlier or an hour later. I said 9.00 or 10.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you adhere by that now?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. Well, I can't be sure of either, whether it was half past 8.00 or 9.00 or -- in any case, that was the case. That's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I won't insist. I assume that you did not pay too much attention to the time. I would like to point another difference to you, also relative to the time, the time when the buses arrived in Ilidza [as interpreted], in Vidikovac, in your interview, this is on page 10 and continues on page 11. You say that that was between 10.00 and 11.00. In the English version, this is on page 41. Did you find it?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you repeat the page numbers?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: 10 and 11, starts at 10 and goes on to 11, if I have noted this well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, it's on page 25. I apologise, I've given you the wrong page number. It's on page 25, and in the English version, it's on page 41.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No objection. I just have a question about the transcript. The question was about buses arriving in Ilidza. I'm not sure if that's right, because the part we are talking about, I think, is the buses arriving at the Hotel Vidikovac if -- unless -- that's what we're talking about on page 41, I believe, and that's in a different town that's in -- I can say the name or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think you need to figure this out amongst yourself, because we don't have it on the screen so it not get --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation], I said Divic -- actually Vidikovac, because that's that, as a matter of fact. My learned friend is absolutely right. I did mention Vidikovac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nicholls, and thank you, Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see the difference?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Would your explanation be similar to the explanation about the previous time period, or do you have another explanation about this difference in times? Yesterday you stated that this was between 8.00 and 9.00, this is on page 21 of yesterday's transcript.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, now, I really don't know. I don't know the exact time. It says 10.00 and 11.00 here. That was the case actually, but now --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can we then conclude that this is a possible time but you did not pay attention to the time of all these events?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is possible. I just gave approximations and it could have been one hour later or one hour earlier. Nobody really --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yesterday, you also stated that you had gotten on the first bus and in your interview you stated that there were security guards on the bus.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor did not ask you anything about the security guards but in your interview you did speak about them, and you said that those were civilian policemen in blue uniforms; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: One more thing I wanted to ask you. Yesterday, you stated that when you arrived in Orahovac, in front of the school with the convoy of buses, you saw some locals there and you go on to say, "Whether the military policemen arrived at the moment, whether they were among the security guards that provided security for the location, I can't remember at this moment." In your interview, you were asked a very specific question. The investigator asked you this: When you arrived in front of the school, whether there were any prisoners there. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Let me repeat the question to avoid any misunderstandings. When you arrived in front of the school, the investigator asked you whether there were any prisoners there already. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: There were no prisoners?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: This is what you stated in the interview, and moreover, when the investigator asked you whether you entered the hall to convince yourself of that, you said, no, but if there had been prisoners you would have seen some guards around the school because somebody would have to guard the prisoners had they been in the school but there were no prisoners in the school. Is that what you answered? Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And you also said at that moment that the security guards that were on the buses, the policemen that were on the buses took the prisoners into the school?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Is that the case?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And finally, you also stated that the military police arrived only about 20 minutes to half an hour later. If you can't remember, I will -- I can jog your memory by telling you on what pages of the transcript you can find this that I'm asking you about. This is on page 31 of your interview in the Serbian language, and page 50 in the English version. This is next to the fourth time your name was mentioned in the transcript of your interview in Serbian. Did you read it?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And let me ask you one more thing. At the time you stated that the buses that were in the convoy were not fully loaded, that the capacity was some 70 to 80 per cent full and that there were some four or five policemen on every bus providing security.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And one more question I would like to ask you. You've also mentioned the presence of a policeman from Bijeljina. Can you please tell me whether he was a military policeman or a civilian policeman?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A civilian policeman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Zivanovic. Who is going next? Mr. Meek? You asked for 45 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Bircakovic. How are you?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I represent Mr. Ljubisa Beara and I'm going to ask you a few questions today which relate to your prior statement to the Office of the Prosecutor and your previous testimony here. Okay?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And if you don't understand the question, would you just tell me that you don't understand it and I'll try to rephrase it. Did you get my question, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay. And is that -- will you do that for me, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay. Now, on the 14th of July, 1995, do you recall what time you went to work that morning?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, maybe 7.00, approximately. That's when I used to come to work.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And just tell us, please, the location, exact location, of where you went to work that morning.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Standard barracks, some three kilometres away from Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And did you have a routine when you went to work in the morning, and if so, was this a normal morning for you when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would come from home, I would go home and then I would drive to the barracks in my own car.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Once you arrived at the barracks, what was the first thing that you would normally do in the morning, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would take the car keys, I would check the car, the oil level, nothing else, nothing particular in any case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And then would you then stay by the car until you were called to go to some location or told to go to some location?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: What would you do then, if you didn't stay with the car?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember whether I was in the cafe where us drivers used to hang around in and have coffee. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Can you give me a more specific location of the cafe where you drivers used to hang around and have coffee within the Standard building?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was on the first floor, to the left from the entrance to the building. Maybe the second office to the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And did it face the street?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Where was the office of Drago Nikolic in regards to -- in relation to your coffee shop?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The second office to the right, the coffee shop was to the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And you've testified that sometime that morning, you received an order from Trbic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And approximately what time did you receive this order?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe around half past 7.00, or 8.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: How was the order communicated to you, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was told to go to the forward command post to fetch Drago Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay. Were you told that -- who told you that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Trbic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: By telephone?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, in person.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay. You left immediately?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And how long had you been a driver with the Zvornik Brigade prior to July 14th, 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe a year or a year and a half.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: As a driver, you would agree with me, sir, that you were -- you were not in a position to have discussions with the superiors that you were driving around; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: So after Mr. Trbic told you, simply told you go fetch Drago, you left immediately, I take it; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And how long did it take you to go to the forward command post, fetch Drago, and return to the Standard building, approximately?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Half an hour at the most, maybe even less.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: So would it be a fair statement that you were back by 8.00 to 8.30, or earlier?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe 8.00 or a bit after 8.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when you got back to the Standard building, was there a gate that you had to drive through?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And were there guards there to open the gate for you?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, but I suppose so. Most probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Then did you drive close to the building and drop off Drago and then go park the car? Would that be normal?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, maybe ten metres or so. This is where I double-parked. I did not always take the car into the garage during the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Do you have any specific recollection, as we speak today, what was the procedure on the 14th of July, 1995, after Mr. Trbic had told you just to go fetch Drago from the forward command post, upon your return?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. To a very large extent.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay. And again, since you seem to have a memory of what occurred when you went through the gate with Drago Nikolic, could you just go ahead and tell me what you did?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, nothing. I left the car. Drago got out of the car, went to the command. I followed him and went upstairs, where coffee is served. That's where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I want to be clear about this. Are you -- is it your testimony under oath that you did not drop off Drago in front of the building and then move the car either ten metres or 20 metres up and park it and then go in? Is that your testimony under oath?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I came by car and stopped maybe ten metres from the entrance. I stopped the car, Drago got out, started walking towards the command. I followed him and entered the building and went upstairs where this cafe was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay. And then I take it that once you stopped the car, Drago got out, you -- he got out first, correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: You then made sure the car was locked up, turned off, in park, and locked, and then you thereafter followed, correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't lock. It wasn't necessary to lock while you were within the perimeter of the barracks. I just got out of the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Do you recall during the interview with the OTP investigator, Dean Manning, on the 13th of day of March, 2002, you do recall that interview, do you not?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And what I want to know, sir, is when was the first time you and Dean Manning had discussed the events which occurred around the 14th, 15th of July, 1995, prior to giving this tape recorded statement?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean did I talk to him?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yeah. When did you talk to him prior to the 13th of March at 9.14 a.m. when the button to the tape recorder got pushed? Was it the night before? Was it the day before? Was it earlier in the morning?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That same day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay. Did you have discussions with Dean Manning before 9.14 in the morning, when he told you on the tape recorded conversation you were summonsed here as a suspect?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Now, you were asked during that interview whether or not Trbic was involved in the meeting, the alleged meeting, which you've discussed, which occurred, to your testimony, on the 14th at the command centre. Do you recall that question?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And do you recall the answer?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said probably the same thing as now, that I don't remember, that I wasn't present and I don't remember whether he did or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: You also indicated to Mr. Manning that you noticed Mr. Nikolic walking into an office and closing the door, correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could I have a page reference, please, excuse me? It might be page 38.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I didn't think it was that far along but you may be right. It is page 38, in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Dean Manning just asked you simply where they met and you said, "In his office," meaning Drago's office?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could I just ask Mr. Meek to point out to me where it says "walking into office and closing the door"?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Well, let me rephrase the question, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: You were asked whether Trbic was present, very simply Dean Manning said, "Was Trbic also present?" Do you remember that question, very simple question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Which page are we on?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: It's page 38 in English. I don't know what in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Page 23 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nicholls, and thank you, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: For the record, Your Honours, that would be 4105.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. Bircakovic, have you read that yet? Have you found that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay. Have you had a chance to review it briefly?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said I didn't know whether Trbic attended.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: That's correct. You did. And you went ahead to tell him because were you in the place, the room where coffee was being made with other drivers to await further orders, correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Then you said, "So when I came up to that place there is a corridor and I saw Drago going into his office." Do you recall that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: You went on to say, "But since it was said that these two people came looking for him, I suppose that they have got in and they were waiting for him and they spoke with him." Isn't that true, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay. Now, afterwards, the meeting lasted 15 to 20 minutes, and you left, correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And were you -- were you completely truthful with Dean Manning on 13th of March, 2002, when you gave this statement?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: You don't know if you told him the truth or lied to him? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what kind of truth you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Well, were you truthful in your answers that you gave to Dean Manning?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay. Now --

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you. You also indicated that those days -- and I think you indicated those days, starting from then, the 14th and the 15th, that you remembered it like through a fog. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not through a fog. Some things are vague. Some things I remember less well, other better.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay. So -- once again, if --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls. One moment, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt, but again I would like a page reference to the fog question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: It's at 25 in English. Mine is on 24 in English, the very bottom of the page. It's probably 25 in English on everybody else's, at the top of the page. I'm not really sure the B/C/S, but if you just scroll to the very top of that page, here we go. There we go, right there. Third line down, and I can read it and maybe they can translate it for him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed, Mr. Meek. I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And again this is being questioned about later on that day, the 14th, you say,"As for Popovic, I'm not sure I remember like through the fog, that he might have been or, indiscernible, I'm not sure about this, it was a very long time ago and a lot of time has gone by. Sometimes I don't even know what has happened today or yesterday." End of quote. Now, do you recall making that statement, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, one moment before you answer, yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just wonder how that question and answer got turned into, You remember the 14th and 15th globally as though through a fog when this again, question was specifically about him remembering Mr. Popovic being at the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Well, I can rephrase the question, Judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I would like him to rephrase them accurately to reflect what the transcript says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I think it's the case of rephrasing it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I'll rephrase it, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I'm not going to rephrase it the way he wants me to, probably, but I will rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Witness, I'm just asking you in this one, two-day period, 14th, 15th of July, isn't it a fair statement that when you gave the interview to Dean Manning back in 2002, five years ago, and seven years after the events, that a lot of what happened in those days were like being in a fog as concerned your memory? Is that true or not?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said -- you understand, some things I know, I do know. Some things I am straining to remember. Some things I'm not sure about, and that's what I call through a fog. That's the way it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Now, in the years that you were a driver for superior officers, would you agree with me, sir, as a common soldier and driver, that it is not common that a person in your position, as such a driver and common soldier, would be told the reason that you were going to fetch somebody or pick someone up or bring another superior officer somewhere, what the purpose of what they were going to do would be?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was not an order back then. When Popovic and Beara arrived at the barracks, everybody saw it. It wasn't concealed. It wasn't being hidden. I was told. Of course, when there are meetings held, then there is no such talk.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Well, was it common or uncommon to be told as a driver that you were to pick up such and such officer for such and such reason or was it just pick up such and such officer?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I was told.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay. And I just want to confirm one thing with you now after your last answer, the one before this, there is nowhere in the, at least in English, 119-page statement you gave to Dean Manning, that you ever mentioned seeing Mr. Popovic and Mr. Beara together at the Standard building that morning?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe he didn't ask me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: He asked you 119 pages of questions and answers, and is it your testimony that because he didn't ask you perhaps, you failed to tell him?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls? Wait one moment, Mr. Bircakovic. Yes, Mr. Nicholls? I don't think this should be discussed in the presence of the witness. Witness, can I ask you to remove your headphones again, please? Well, I am just -- I've taken this measure in anticipation of what I think you could be saying. If he is not going to say what is in my mind, then obviously we'll get the witness to put his headphones back. Yes, Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: It's just again not a particularly accurate characterisation of the interview as a whole, because on page 115 there is a question, Manning: "Do you recall after the meeting on the 14th July in the morning, when is the last time you saw -- the next time you saw Beara?" And then there is an answer after that, he didn't come, I didn't see him, so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But the question that Mr. Meek put to the witness is whether throughout the entire interview, he ever affirmed seeing Popovic and Beara together, and the suggestion is that he never did, so much so that the witness has understood that and tried to give an explanation by way of, Maybe I was never asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I understand that, but the question or if you say to somebody, When was the next time you saw X after you saw him on the 14th and he says, Well, not again, and doesn't correct that, it's -- I think it's not fair to say that the witness never mentioned it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But it's not being suggested to the witness that he never said that he saw Beara. What is being suggested is that he never said that he saw Popovic and Beara together. Correct me if I'm wrong, Mr. Meek, because I don't want to interpret your question any differently from the way you put it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Both, Your Honour, that he never saw my client, nor did he see my client with Mr. Zivanovic's client.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So your remark holds good insofar as that. So why don't you break the two questions, the question into two questions, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I could do that, Judge, but since Mr. Nicholls has been so helpful for us, maybe he could point out to us where in the transcript prior to page 115 that this witness told Dean Manning that he saw Mr. Beara that morning, because the question says, on Manning's part, Do you recall after the meeting in the morning when was the last time you saw -- or the next time you saw Beara? So that's a leading suggestive question. Maybe Mr. Nicholls, helpful as he is, can point out where this witness ever said he saw, laid his eyes on, Mr. Beara. It would be very simple. We could move on, because it didn't happen, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Do you wish to comment on that, Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yeah. He can do his own cross and read the statement himself, but the witness here was asked when was the next time you saw him as though the understanding from Mr. Manning from the previous 114 pages of text was, You've talked about Mr. Beara being there, you saw that -- and took it as you saw him there, and the witness then says, Well the next time was X.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Perhaps I can leave it in your hands, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I think he ought to be fair with the Court, Judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honour, all --

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I think he ought to be fair with the Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: My objection and all I'm asking is that he be accurate when he tells the witness what is in the transcript and he hasn't been now, this is number 3, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's not make an issue out of it. I think let's keep the calm, all of us. I suggest that you break the question into parts and put it to the witness. We've got -- I know that according to the schedule, we've got seven minutes left, but we need to break at 15.40 in two minutes' time, so if you prefer to leave this till after the break, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Judge, I -- I'd prefer if we have 2 minutes, anyway, till break to leave it, and I have one other suggestion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: This witness, he has the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Version in front of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I would ask you -- or him, and maybe you need to order it, to look through there and read it and see if there is at any time he ever mentioned any time seeing, laying eyes on Mr. Beara that morning, that's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Exactly. I think that can be addressed now before we break, by yourself. Yes, Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I object to that, Your Honour, because we gave the witness a transcript yesterday to read. He's had an opportunity to read it, and I think the witness may need a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, but on --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: It's a long transcript. It's 115 pages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: On the strength of that, he should be in a position to answer the question. So --

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: May I just ask one question before --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, just ask one question and we'll have a break. Wait until the witness has got his earphones back, headphones back. Yes, go ahead, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Witness, when you were describing to Dean Manning in March of 2002 the events of the morning of July 14th, 1995, you never one time told him that you had seen him with your own eyes at the Standard. Isn't that correct? Him being Mr. Beara.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stated that Popovic and Beara attended the meeting, and it's written there, Who was present at the meeting? Popovic and Beara. Was Trbic there as well? Answer: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: One more question --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We have to stop --

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: -- before the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We have to stop here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: One more question before -- if you don't mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: You also said, didn't you, Mr. Bircakovic, that again to the question as to who was ordering this operation to kill people, and you say you know that well -- "You know that well." I'm on page 24 English. "There was a command, the may command. You understand since Beara and Popovic there, you understand that they probably came here to order this, because I don't know for certain since Drago was subordinate to Popovic and I can only make assumptions." You also stated after that, when again talking about whether Trbic was in the meeting, you said you didn't know who was in that room because you weren't there. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't go in, but in the morning, when I arrived, Popovic and Beara arrived as well, so they went into the barracks and I saw them go in. After sometime, Trbic approached me and told me, "Go tell Drago at the forward command post that he's being summoned to a meeting." And I was asked was it possible that the command didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: We have to take a break, but I'm going to ask the witness to take the statement back and to review it, so he can show me where he ever told Dean Manning what he just testified to, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. We'll need to have a 30-minute break because one of us has a meeting. Yes, Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Very minor point. It says "may command" in the transcript, in the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's come to it later --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- because there is a meeting at very short notice. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I notice -- I note both Mr. Meek and Mr. Nicholls standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I just have a small point. Mr. Meek read back a portion of the transcript, page 32, line 5, and it states -- transcript of the interview and it states in the trial transcript may command, m-a-y. That is what it states in the interview transcript. It's actually a typo, it's actually main, m-a-i-n, command. That's correct in the other transcript that was provided to the Defence in English, but I just wanted to make that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Point taken by you, as well, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. Bircakovic, have you had a chance to review the statement that you gave to Dean Manning?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And you'll agree with me that you never told Dean Manning that you visually observed Mr. Beara at the command post there in Zvornik command, on the 14th of July in the morning, did you, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no such a question, and therefore I couldn't answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Well, sir, I'd like to draw your attention to page 19 of that interview, and in B/C/S -- I'm not sure what page in B/C/S it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I think it's probably pages, I don't know exactly where on 19 or 20, but it's probably page 12 to 13, thereabouts, in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Sir, could you look at page 12 to 13 with me, in the B/C/S? Now, Witness, I'd like to just draw your attention to the very long statement by Dean Manning that starts,"I'm going to ask you questions about the killings and about organisation for killings of many thousands of men." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. Manning then goes on and he tells you, "Firstly, I want you to understand some things. We have part of witnesses to the killings. We have survivors who were put -- or who were part of the execution, who were shot at. We have aerial images of the executions taking place. We have seized records from the Zvornik Brigade and the Bratunac Brigade and we've had many people from those brigades and the Drina Corps interviewed. We have your MP logs. "I want you to understand that it's very important for you to tell the truth. If you try and hide what happened or hide your part in what happened, or your knowledge of what happened, I can prove that you're lying. And I want you to understand that this is your chance to tell the truth here now. "I personally exhumed the bodies of thousands and thousands of men and boys from Kozluk, from Branjevo military farm, from the dom above the factory in Karakaj, from the Pilici dom, from the Kravica warehouse and from Orahovac. "And as I said, I want to ask you questions about that, but before -- or before I ask you specific questions, I'd like to give you the opportunity of telling me what happened, remembering that I have all those things, all that knowledge. We even have your vehicle logs." Then Mr. Manning goes on and he says to you, "Now, can you tell me what you know to have happened?" And your answer, sir, was, what? The very first sentence is all I'd like you to say.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I'll tell you what I know."

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay. And wouldn't you agree with me, sir, that after investigator Manning put forth the entire theory of the OTP's case to you and then allowed you to tell him what you know happened, that that was a very broad statement, wasn't it, sir, very broad question?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And you even tell him, "I can tell you what I know." When you told him that, sir, were you telling him the truth or not?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: But thereafter, thereafter, for the next, I don't know, 160 pages, you never told him that you physically with your own eyes saw my client, Mr. Beara, at the Standard building that morning, did you, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I repeat: There was no such a question. Where can you see a question put to this effect, Did you see this or the other person there?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I can either do it on redirect, but I think it would make more sense now, I think given that the question has just happened, the witness's whole answer to that broad question ought to be read into the record. I can do it later, but I think it makes sense.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We think that we can proceed, Mr. Nicholls, okay, and you can deal with it directly on redirect.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Later on, Mr. Manning asked you a specific question and that was, again on the same page, "Was Beara at the school on the 14th?" Do you recall that question?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And you basically said, "I think he was, I'm not sure, I don't think he was."

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: So did it ever occur to you when you earlier told this investigator, "I'll tell you all I know," and then he later asked you specifically if Mr. Beara was at the school on the 14th, it never dawned on you to tell him that you had seen him earlier in the morning at the Standard building?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those are two different things. The school is one thing and the other place is another thing. He asked me about the school, whether I saw him in front of the school. I said no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And when was it, sir, that it dawned on you that you had seen, back on the 14th of July, 1995, Mr. Beara in the morning at the Standard building? When did that occur to you, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When did it occur to me? Hmm. What do you mean? What do you mean by that, when it occurred to me?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: What I mean, sir, is apparently it didn't occur to you to tell Dean Manning that you had visually observed Mr. Beara there that morning at the Standard, even though you had told him you would truthfully tell him everything you knew, and it didn't dawn on you to tell him that you had seen Mr. Beara at the Standard building earlier in the morning on the 14th, when he specifically asked you had you seen him later in the day at the school, correct so far?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The question was whether he was seen by the school. I said no. He did not ask me anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay. So again, if it didn't dawn on you then and it didn't dawn on you five years later in 2002, or five years after the events --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm objecting to the way these questions are being put that it dawned on him. The witness has explained that he wasn't asked before or during the interview and he's answered it as best he can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Beside the issue of the language used, whether it should be the -- whether it's the right choice of words or not, but we are here convinced that you've laboured this point enough, we've heard enough, and that you should move to something different.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge. I'd like to put on e-court, if I could, 65 ter 296 and if they could do the English and B/C/S side by side. It appears that we have the original B/C/S of that document on the right but we still have some transcript on the left. Is there a possibility -- okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Witness, do you see in front of you a document that was spoken about yesterday, that you talked about yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: That's the vehicle log, work logbook from 1 July until 31 July 1995, correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And that was for the Opel Rekord, R-e-k-o-r-d, that you drove and you testified about yesterday, correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the page following that, could we see that, please? Now, the Prosecutor took some pains with you yesterday to have you justify why it was that on the 14th day - and we'll get to that in a moment - on the 14th of July, that the route under column 4, being the forward command post, the IKM, was never placed on that date as a location that you drove, correct? Do you recall that testimony?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Now, we see on this document that's on the screen that on 4th day of July, 1995, you put down that you were at Standard, IKM, Bratunac, correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And on the 5th of July, you have Standard, IKM, Zvornik, correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Then on the 12th of July, you have Zvornik, Osmace, Standard, IKM, and Baljkovica, correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And also on the 13th of July, you noted that you drove Standard, IKM, Zvornik and local, didn't you, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Well, what do you mean it's possible? It's on there, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I mean is yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Is that also what you meant when I asked you about the 12th of July, where it shows that the car you had gone to Zvornik, Osmace, Standard, IKM and Baljkovica? Because your answer on the transcript says "possible" again.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay. Before we get off this document, I notice that you have the 24th July 1995, after the 13th July 1995. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Can we just go to page 4 or 5, I think it would be, same document. That would be ERN number 03075156. I'm sorry. I'm sorry. The --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: It would be ERN 03075154. That's the English. The B/C/S would be ERN 00694701.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And that's page 3 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. Bircakovic, will you take a look at that, please, and at the B/C/S, that's again vehicle work log from 14 July until 31 July 1995 for the same car, correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay. Then if we go to page 5, and perhaps 6 -- 5 would be in English, I think, at ERN number 03075155, and the -- try the next page. That's good. Now if we could find the corresponding in B/C/S, 00694702. You see it, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: On the 22nd of July you also have noted that you were at Standard, IKM, Boskovici, correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: But it jumps from the 22nd of July to the 23rd of July, and as we saw from the other document, you have the 24th day of July on the document we just looked at. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Can you explain this, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is there to explain? There is nothing but a date. There is no route, no signature, nothing. This is a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: But it wasn't a mistake on the document you're looking at for 14 July 1995 on the route you took, is there?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is missing is the route. For example, there is no forward command post recorded for the 14th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And also, real quickly while we are on that, July -- 14 July, apparently you carried five people that day, according to you, correct? Can you name them? You understand my question? You drove five people that day, on the 14th. Can you tell me the names of them, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where to? What five people? What are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I'm talking about if you look at the B/C/S version, it would be --

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: -- where it says, total carried, tonnes and people, it would be -- 8 would be the line you're under, column 8.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's why -- it's just a figure of writing, to put it that way. Because, for the following day there is nothing, and still the car went places on those two days. I don't know why this was recorded in this particular way. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: You also have under number of journeys for the 14th, just one journey, correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you can call it so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I spoke about these travel orders. These travel orders, you can't really rely on them because they were not kept very accurately. They would -- records would be made on two or three days, then nothing, then there would be a certain mileage on the milometer and then destinations were sought that would fit into a certain mileage, and they were filled out as if the car went there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Well, are you saying, then, that this is just a falsified record?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, things were as they were. That's how things were done at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay. So things were done at the time, falsifying records was no big deal to you, correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not falsifying. That's how things were done. People were aware of that. That's what I think. I don't know. That's how things were entered.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Well, sir, if they're not true, they're false. Would you agree with me on that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what do I know? I don't know. I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Well, you know the difference between the truth and a lie?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Okay. And you don't know the difference between something being correct and something being false? Is that what you're telling the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just want to say that that's the way it was done. It's written in that order. And that's just the way it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Let me just ask you this, then, sir: How difficult would it have been for you to just put down that you went to -- from Standard to the IKM and then back to Standard, if that's what you did?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but maybe two or three days passed before it was entered, but why? It wasn't a problem. It wasn't being hidden. It was known that Drago was at the forward command post, that a car came to fetch him. There is the duty officer's logbook. These are all known things.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Sir, you can say all those things, but it certainly isn't known from your vehicle logbook, is it?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you again, that's the way it was done then. It can't be changed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I understand that what you're telling me that it was a common practice for you to falsify these records, but my question to you, sir, is this vehicle logbook, work and vehicle, machine and generator logbook, showing the 14th, would not indicate that you drove to the forward command post. Is that -- would you agree with me, on the 14th?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think he has already stated, he answered that several times, both yesterday and today.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And I'm going to ask you to go over to number 8 again and tell me why it was, if you can remember, you would put five people being in that car with you that day, when under your testimony, it was only Drago Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Would that just be another example of falsifying things, the way things were done back then?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not falsified. That's how it was written at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Well, sir, I'm going to suggest to you that you never saw Ljubisa Beara on the 14th in the morning at the Standard building, as you first testified about today because he was not there, he was at Black River on the 13th and the 14th. And I put it to you, sir, that you are not speaking the truth here, just like you didn't speak the truth on these exhibits, on the logbooks, because it means nothing to you to tell the truth or to tell a lie. Isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I don't have any further questions for this witness, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Mr. Meek. I have next the Nikolic Defence team. You asked for an hour and a half. Do you still require an hour and a half? Mr. Bourgon?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President. I hope to be shorter than an hour and a half. I will try to do -- finish that within an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead. We'll have the next break as usual, at quarter to 6.00. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Bircakovic. I do have a series of questions for you and I understand that this can be -- you probably are quite tired by now. I will try to move as swiftly as possible, and you'll be glad to hear that most of my questions is simply to get you to confirm things that you stated in your statement. And I will leave it at that other than a few -- for a few questions. My first question doesn't come from your statement. I'd just like to know whether you know Major Galic, who was working at the Zvornik Brigade command.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
