utterances.text: Go ahead, because we can follow -- but we've lost one monitor, computer, completely. It says "no connection, check signal cable." At least on mine, that's the message I'm having. I see that my colleagues have got the same problem but in the meantime, if you proceed, we can follow the transcript on the other -- on LiveNote. What we won't be able to do for the time being, unless this is adjusted, is to watch any documents, see any documents, that you may ask to be shown to the witness, but not as they are being shown. So go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I do not intend to show documents at least for the first part of the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Getting back to where we were, Mr. Bircakovic, your response to my first question was that you did know Major Galic, and I'd like to know if -- whether it is correct that you drove him many times to visit battalions and that, indeed, you knew him quite well. Is that a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And would it also be a fair statement that Major Galic would know you pretty well because you drove him to visit battalions?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, can you think of a reason, Mr. Bircakovic, why Mr. Galic would say that he does not recall who you are by name and that he doesn't know what you were a driver assigned to Drago Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: For the sake of the record, I was referring to the transcript on page 10648, lines 16 to 25, on the 27th of April. My questions now, Mr. Bircakovic, will be focusing on your interview with the Prosecution, and I think you said that already, but you recall that this interview took place more than five years ago. Can you confirm this?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And during your interview, you stated that in response -- well, there was a question asked by my colleague from the Prosecution and something you stated in the interview, and you were asked questions about Jasikovac, who was the commander of the military police; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the commander of the military police company.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And when you responded to my colleague, you stated that Mr. Jasikovac was reporting to Drago Nikolic, who was the head of security. Now, I'd also like to simply read you a part of your interview and ask you whether you can tell me if that is correct. Now, that was from page 14 in English. If there is a need, we can show it to you, but I don't believe it will be necessary. It's a short part of your interview. And it reads like this: "And who did he report to? Who was above him in the chain of command?" Your response was the following: "I think he was reporting to Drago Nikolic, who was head of the security, and he was also subordinate to the commander of the brigade because the brigade commander could give any orders that could not be revoked by anybody else." Do you agree with this statement today?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And you also said in your interview that the person who was really giving us, military policemen, orders was indeed Jasikovac; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, if I go to your statement -- your statement or your interview, you stated something about being the driver for Drago Nikolic, and I will quote exactly what you stated and ask you to confirm. And that was on page 17 in the English version, when you were talking about your duties as driver. I quote - it's from line 7 down on page 17 in English, and then you said, "Then it was decided that this car could not be assigned exclusively to the chief of security, and then this car was used to drive around operatives and those who were in charge of going and checking on the battalions and go in the field." Can you confirm that this was correct, that this car was not exclusively assigned to Drago Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And would it be a fair statement to say that no permission was required either from yourself or from Drago Nikolic for another operations officer to use this car?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And the keys to this car --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No objection. Sorry to interrupt. I'm just having trouble finding an earlier reference in the interview transcript when my colleague said, You also said in your interview that the person who was really giving us military policemen orders was indeed Jasikovac. If I could have a reference when possible I would appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, if you could help us there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I'm doing my best, Mr. President, and I'm really sorry that -- I had the reference on page 16 in the English version and I will quote so this way, it will go on the record. The question was: "I'm not sure because they had the meetings up there regarding the matters and we were not given any direct orders from above. It was our company commander who was giving us orders."

utterances.speaker: MR. MANNING
utterances.text: "Okay. Who was your company commander?" Your answer was: "Jasikovac, Mijo." Is that sufficient for my colleague?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yeah. I just wanted the page. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Let us proceed, Mr. Bircakovic, so that we can finish as quickly as we can. I believe my last questions I wanted to ask you was that the keys to this car, the car that you were driving, as well as the keys to all of the cars that belonged to the Zvornik Brigade, you could find those keys in the office of the duty officer right up on the wall; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Partly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Why partly? Could you explain?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, maybe sometimes keys would be forgotten or something like that. Something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: But the proper procedure would be for the keys to be there and whoever would use the car, that's where they would pick up the keys; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Moving on to the 14th of July, in the morning, it is my understanding from your testimony over the past two days that the reason you went to fetch Drago Nikolic at the forward command post, the IKM, was because you were told that Popovic and Beara were looking for him. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And I'd like to know when you went to get Drago Nikolic at the forward command post to take him to Standard, in response to a question by my colleague, you said that it was about a 30 minutes drive. I'd like to know, did you drive by the Orahovac school or did you use that other road that you were talking about during your testimony? If you recall, of course.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think I went through Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And do you recall if you saw any activity going on in Orahovac at that time?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Should I take this that there was no activity or you did not -- or you're not sure?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember anything happening. It was normal.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I move on now to what happened following the meeting at the Zvornik Brigade command, and you've mentioned in response to my colleague in the first day, that of course you did not attend that meeting and you don't know what went on in that meeting; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, coming out of the meeting, there is something you said in your interview, and I will quote exactly what you said, and that is on page 20 in the English version, I will just read it, it's quite short. It goes like this: "After that, Drago Nikolic" -- well, maybe I should read a bit up. It goes like this: "I went to fetch Drago, brought him to the command centre, and he was there in the command but I do not know what they were talking about there." Now, the part I'm interested in is the following one: "After that, Drago Nikolic then told me that there would be some people coming in for exchange and these people were just sent to him, and he did not know anything about that beforehand, so they were just shipped over to him." Can you confirm what you said during your interview?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And then you went on to say, and again I will quote from the interview, "At the beginning, he was very angry when he came out of the meeting that was held in the command centre, because he was not consulted beforehand but was only ordered to find some accommodation for these people." Can you also confirm that this is what you said and that you still agree with this statement today?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, it's also my understanding from reading your interview that what Drago Nikolic told you about finding or being ordered to find some accommodation for these people, he never mentioned anything about killings at that time, did he?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I take this as being that he did not mention anything about killings. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did not, right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, in fact, this is something that you confirmed in your interview, because it was suggested to you by Mr. Manning, and I quote now from page 35 of the English transcript, towards the end, where Mr. Manning said, "That was an order to kill." And your response was, "I don't know. I wasn't there. But if I had been there, and if that was the case, I would have told you." Do you recall saying this to Mr. Manning during your interview?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And from your testimony, I take it that shortly after this meeting, you went to motel Vidikovac and that was because Drago Nikolic had been ordered to go there to wait for the buses; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: But you did not go into the hotel, you just waited for the buses; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we waited outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And that's when you were told to sit in one of those buses and then Drago left with the car; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, in your interview, you were asked by Mr. Manning what you thought you were doing when you left in that bus, and I will read what your answer was, and that was from page 46 of the interview, towards the middle of the page. The question by Mr. Manning was the following: "What did you think you were doing when you left on the bus to Orahovac?" And your answer was: "I wasn't thinking anything. I was just supposing, as I supposed the others were assuming, that these people are being taken to be located in the school, accommodated in the school, and then there would be some kind of an exchange as we used to do before, or something like that." Do you recall this answer and confirm the same today?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Would I be right in saying that at that moment, you were told that you were going to Orahovac but you knew nothing about any other prisoners or detainees that were to be taken to other schools? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, once you're on that bus, there is something that wasn't covered at all during your interview -- or your examination-in-chief, or maybe I missed it, but you stated that on those buses were people in uniform, civilian police wearing blue uniforms, and that these people were escorting the buses. Can you confirm this?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And would I be right in saying that you did not know from which unit these civilian policemen were from, and that you did not speak to them?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: A further question was put to you by Mr. Manning, whether you saw anything in front of the column that approached Vidikovac motel. I'll be very precise and I'll simply ask you, did you by any chance see a carrier, an armed carrier, which is white with the letters "UN" on it? Did you see anything like that in front of those buses on that day?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, these people, and you responded to a question from my colleague that they are the ones who let the prisoners out and escorted them in the gym, I'd simply like to confirm what you stated, that these were people wearing uniforms of the civilian police, that they had camouflage uniforms, and that there may have been as many as 10 or 15 but you were not able to say exactly how many because of all the mass of people that gathered around the gym. Would that be a fair illustration of your words?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, you yourself, I'm not sure if you did say this, but I think that it is important, you yourself never went into that gym, did you?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And you were further asked during your interview whether, in the few days before the 14th, whether you drove to that school or other schools in the Zvornik area, and your response was that before the prisoners were brought, we did not drive to Orahovac school. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, to make it clear for the transcript, I take it that there were no preparations that were made of any schools in the Zvornik area before what you were privy to on the 14th of July. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, you testified earlier today that when you arrived in Orahovac with that bus that you were on, there were no prisoners in the gym. What I'd like to know from you is, the persons you saw positioned around this area, that's where you saw some of your fellow military policemen from the Zvornik Brigade who were doing the security around the school; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, according to the information which is in our possession, it is our understanding that the military police from the Zvornik Brigade, what they were doing that day was to provide security around the school and that none of the military policemen were involved into the killings which took place on that day. My question to you is: Do you have any information that would suggest otherwise?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: When Trbic arrived with some others, they were also providing security around the school; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, I take it that at some point in time, shortly after, Drago Nikolic arrived at the school, and it's my understanding from your interview that by the time he arrived, the prisoners had just been brought into the gym and they were not yet being loaded on any trucks. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And would it be a fair statement to say that at that time there were quite a few people around the school, women, children and locals, and that everybody was very curious as to what was happening in that school?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And Drago Nikolic, when he arrived, he was coming from the direction of Zvornik, he parked the car, you've already said that before, and he gave you the keys. What I'd like to confirm is at that point he met with Jasikovac, according to your interview. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And again, according to your interview, you were not aware what Drago Nikolic and Jasikovac discussed at that time?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And whether -- neither Jasikovac, nor Drago Nikolic, to your knowledge, went into the school or the gym; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And according to your interview, Drago Nikolic stayed in Orahovac not very long, and in fact, one hour or less, maybe 45 minutes. Now, this, for the sake of my colleague, comes from page 59 in the English version of your interview. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And when he arrived, he was driving the car he usually uses, that's the Opel Rekord, and according to your interview, he did not bring anything with him; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And no one was with Drago Nikolic, and it was suggested to you, or it was asked of you, whether the situation changed at the school when he arrived, and your response on page 60 of the English version was that, no, nothing changed. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And then on page 64 of your interview, in the English version, Mr. Manning asked you the following question: "Okay. Let's go back; he first arrives." Now we are talking about Drago Nikolic. "He goes away, he comes back a second time." Question: "Was he present when the prisoners were being loaded on to the trucks? You were present. Was he?" Your answer was: "I think he was not." Can you confirm that this is so, that Drago Nikolic was not there when the prisoners were being loaded on the trucks?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, moving on to the first time you saw Drago Nikolic, you've already testified to the fact that you did not see him for the entire day, and you don't know where he was during that time. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, talking about those trucks, I'd just like you to confirm that any truck you saw being loaded with prisoners, they were approaching all the way to the door, they would back up and then some of the prisoners would be taken on board these trucks. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And to make it clear, none of the prisoners were taken out of the gym and then loaded into a truck that would have stayed on the street; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, you yourself, you testified that you went behind those trucks as some kind of an escort. I'd like you to confirm that it took some time before you were asked to follow any of these trucks. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, maybe after an hour or so.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And the area where you turned around, you did not see anything which was going on on the other side of the railway; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So in fact you never drove to that area where the killings you learned later took place; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not on that day. Maybe two or three months later, or maybe a month later.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And you never took Drago Nikolic to that area on that day either, did you?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, a question was put to you as to who was responsible for the military policemen from the Zvornik Brigade once Drago Nikolic left after being there for about 45 minutes, and your response on page 27 and 28 was that you don't know exactly who was in charge but that Jasikovac was there. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, moving on to later on that night, you testified that you drove by the water point when it was dark, along with Drago Nikolic, and that you saw bodies in the meadow as you were driving to Kitonjice. I'd like you to confirm that at that time there was nobody present at that location and no activity going on whatsoever. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, when you were escorting these -- your previous answer, Mr. Bircakovic, was missed in the transcript. I can either repeat the question or you can just -- that there was nobody present at that location and no activity whatsoever when you drove by later that night. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, when you -- when you were following those trucks on a few occasions, you did this and other than for the occasion about this policeman from Bijeljina, you were alone in that vehicle; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: In response to a question by my colleague representing Mr. Popovic, you stated that there was at one point a policeman from Bijeljina who accompanied you once or twice on following those trucks; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And you stated that this man was not from your territory because, indeed, he was from Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, I'm not sure I understood from your interview, and I will quote the words that is on page 67 and 68, of the interview, where you stated that, "He was down there and then he was with me for a while. So whether he did that or not, I would not know." The best thing, I believe, is just in your own words, can you say what you know about this civilian policeman from Bijeljina? Where was he and where did he go, from what you recall?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Allegedly, his brother was imprisoned in Srebrenica and he had arrived to ask these people whether they knew anything about it. That would be that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So just for the sake of to be clear, did he always stay at the school and was with you or did he go to that area where you later learned that killings were taking place?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On one or two occasions, he went with me, and then he got out by the school there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And I'm not sure I understand. I'm sorry. I'd just like you confirm, did he go to the area where killings took place at any point in time, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, in terms of following those trucks, which you said you did on a few occasions, would I be right in saying that you did not see any other Zvornik Brigade military policemen do the same as you did? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And sometimes the trucks were escorted where at other times there was no escort with these trucks; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And Cedo Jovic, for example, did not escort any trucks and you only saw him in front of the school at one point; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, yesterday in response to a question by my colleague from the Prosecution, the question was about the number of prisoners which could fit on one truck, your response, and I quote from page 11026, lines 11 to 15, on the basis of the size of the trucks, you said "perhaps 20 or 30, I don't know exactly." I'd just like you to confirm that indeed you cannot establish with any degree of precision how many people could fit in one of those trucks; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I have one more question and then we can actually -- actually, we can break now, Mr. President. I think it's the time. Someone has indicated to me that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We still have another 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Sorry. I was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If you --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: No, no, no. I'm pretty -- I'm on a roll. Everything's okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Mr. Bircakovic, just a few more minutes and then we will go for the break. I take it from your -- from what you could see when you followed those trucks on a few occasions, that everything was peaceful and that the prisoners themselves -- I mean, they didn't offer any resistance or anything. There was no obstruction from the prisoners; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true, there was no resistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, of course, you can't put yourself in the shoes of the prisoners, but would it be a fair statement to say that they believed that they were going to be exchanged? In your view?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I object to that. How could he possibly answer what was in the mind of any individual prisoner on that truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: From what he saw, Mr. President, he can draw his own conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'll withdraw the objection. It's just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead. Are you in a position to answer that question, Mr. Bircakovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I believe that they were being taken for an exchange. What they thought, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. So there was --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you for your candour, Mr. Bircakovic, and we'll move on. You were asked during your interview, and I quote from page 72, whether you knew who was at the execution point, and your answer was, no. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, in line to a previous answer from one of my questions, I take it that you have no knowledge whatsoever about any military policemen from the Zvornik Brigade going to the execution point on that day. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, you testified yesterday that before driving to the forward command post with Drago Nikolic that night, that you spent about 30 minutes at the school or that Drago Nikolic spent about 30 minutes at the school, while in your interview - that was on page 64 - you stated that this took place after the prisoners were taken to the execution point. So let me try and make that more precise as a question. When you went with Drago Nikolic, there were no more prisoners being taken to the execution point; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. When Drago arrived in the evening, when he returned.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So when he returned, there were no more executions going on; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Again, let's clarify. "No" what? Do you agree that when Drago Nikolic returned in the evening, there were no more executions going on? If you agree you say, "Yes, I agree."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: The next part I'd like to cover, Mr. Bircakovic, is concerning the machinery that you saw that night, and I would simply like you to confirm that when you saw that machinery stopped at the school and move towards the execution point, or whatever you saw about that machinery, this also took place before you drove with Drago Nikolic to the forward command post on that night. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And driving beside the water point, you did not stop, those bodies were visible from the road, is that so?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. That was a reflection from the car.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And at that point in time, and from -- based on your interview, you yourself did not say anything to Drago Nikolic driving by the water point, is that so?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He answered that question yesterday, neither of them, neither he nor Nikolic said anything, but if you want to push it further, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: It's a lead-up to my following question, Mr. President. I'd like the witness to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: -- even say it again, even though it was -- I realise it was asked before. There's not too many of those questions that were asked before, so I'd like your -- your indulgence, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Mr. Bircakovic, can you confirm that, driving which that water point at that time in the evening, that you did not say anything to Drago Nikolic and that Drago Nikolic was also quiet and he did not say anything?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, I wanted to confirm this because I'd like to just quote your interview and I quote now from page 82 of your interview because you were kind of asked why it was so that nobody was saying a word. And on page 82, and I quote what you said here, "We never discussed of his orders or what had been his orders from the higher instances. Anyway, it was visible that he was very angry. He was constantly silent. He was not saying anything, and it was not my thing to do - or to - to do that. He is my superior officer." Is that a fair illustration of how sinister the atmosphere was that night?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And that's when you return and you drop Drago Nikolic at the gate, you went to park the car, and you went home. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, based on your previous answers, because at some point you said that it could have been around 8.00, 8.30 at night, is it possible that it was indeed much later than 8.00, 8.30, that the time is not really what is important, it's the sequence of events? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was dark. It was already night. Whether it was 9.00 or what, in any case, it was dark. The lights had to be turned on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, in your interview, and I quote from page 78, not quote, I just say what happened there on page 78. You stated that during the time you were in Orahovac, what was happening was a shock for all the people who were there and that this were no discussions either during or afterwards. Is that a fair statement of what happened?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: The next area with my questions will move on to Pilica. I think, Mr. President, if -- with your --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Before you move that, but about the time, we're talking of July, summer, halfway through summer, basically, and to my knowledge, at 8.30 in the evening, it's still light during the month of July. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, yes, but I said 9.00 or even after 9.00. In any case, it was dark. I don't know how late it was. But it was dark.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. That's important to establish. Yes. What were you about to say, Mr. Bourgon?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Well, I suggest to break now because I'm moving into another area which is Pilica, another area, from now on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. So we'll have a 25-minute break starting from now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bourgon?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Welcome back, Mr. Bircakovic. I hope you had a chance to rest and we'll try to finish as quickly as I can. As I mentioned just before the break, I'd like to move to a different area and that is Pilica, and you testified already that you went to Pilica with Jasikovac and that was later than the events in Orahovac; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And you also said in your interview that you in fact dropped Jasikovac at Pilica a short while and that you were able to confirm that there were prisoners held in the school; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, something that did not come out yet is the people that were guarding those prisoners, you stated in your interview that the people guarding them "were not our people, I think security was different." Now I quote from page 84 of the English transcript for my colleague. I'd like you to confirm that indeed you were not sure whether these people were from Zvornik Brigade or not. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And once again, I'd like you to confirm that you yourself did not go into the school and that even Jasikovac remained outside discussing some things with the people there. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, with respect to what happened to the people who were held in Pilica, would I be correct in saying that you only learned later, when you were listening to the radio or TV, and you heard about what was done, and you mention in your interview that it is when Erdemovic confessed that you really learned what happened there? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And again to confirm that Drago Nikolic was not in Pilica with you, is that so?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, with respect to Rocevic, a different area, you stated that to the best of your recollection, when you took Jasikovac there, you don't think there was anybody else there. There was only the security or the army that was there, to use your words from page 89 of the interview. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know how you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Mr. Bircakovic, let's just go back, because there is one answer that I'd like to make clear, just to avoid any uncertainty. A little earlier I said and again to confirm that Drago Nikolic was not in Pilica with you, is that so? Can you please answer yes, he was not there, if that is your answer?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. He wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, let me take that last question over again, concerning the people in Rocevic. Now, I will quote from page 89 of the interview, and this will make things easier. The question at the end of page 88 was, "Was anyone else with you, Jasikovac and yourself, anyone else?" Your response was, "I don't think there was anybody else. There was only the security, the army that was there." Now then the question was asked of you, "Who was guarding the prisoners, which part of the army?" And your response was, "I'm not sure from which battalion they came directly, but they were also officers. "Were they from Zvornik Brigade's officers?" Answer: "It is possible that they were. They might not have been. I'm not sure that I know that for certain." Do you recall these were your answers and confirm that you stand by your answers today?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And in Rocevic, Jasikovac did get out of the car to go and speak to the people but you did not see with whom he spoke, is that so?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know those people.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And there was the issue of those prisoners and something that would have happened to them in Kozluk. Would I be right in saying that you only heard about this later, after a while? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, I need to go back to the issue of the vehicle logs, and I hate to labour the point. Now, of course I can't speak for the accused but if other people in the courtroom had been in the army they could understand much better your answers but let me just try to make it clear for everyone, in terms of how these vehicle logs are filled in. First I'd like to confirm with you that what you stated is that the vehicle logs themselves, because of the way they were filled, they are not fully accurate as to the places where the cars went on a particular day. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And you also stated that it was a common practice, that wasn't only you, that was a common practice for all drivers to fill in the logs not on the exact day but a few days later, sometimes many days later. Is that a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And the reason the drivers fill in these vehicle logs at different points in time is because it is important to justify the number of kilometres and also the fuel that is used, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And would I be right in saying that this is particularly important at the end of the month, and that's when, if there is anything missing in those logs, it is then filled in so that the record is complete for the month? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, with the number of kilometres crossed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, let's look at the P296, the vehicle log, just to ask you a few questions so that you can confirm. Is your screen working, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, now it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Mine is not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just press one of the buttons, except the off, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I didn't press the off, but I don't have anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You don't have it either? We didn't have it for some time but I was patient waiting for it to be solved.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Ah, here we go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is it okay now?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I pressed e-court on mine and it worked, so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, okay. Is it working now? All right. Mr. Nikolic? Go ahead, Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Mr. Bircakovic, can you just confirm the last column on the document that is before you, I believe it says "manager's signature." Who is it that would sign there?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the most part, Drago Nikolic would sign.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Even if this column called "manager's signature"? Maybe I misunderstood your testimony from yesterday. Do you recognise the signature that is there before you now in that last column?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, maybe turn the page. I don't know whether this is the Nikolic, because there was one Nikolic in the logistics. Can we turn to the next page?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Actually, the one he testified upon yesterday was another page.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: My question, Mr. Bircakovic, is on that page where it says "manager's signature," are you aware that this would be signed not by the user but by someone in the transport section? Because this is about the fuel and the oil use. Are you aware of this or you're not familiar with this first page?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Right. That's the person who issued the fuel for vehicles for that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, while we are on this page, in the top part just above this section, where your name is written, where it says Bircakovic, Milorad, there are also two other names there. Can you confirm what these two -- whose names these are and why these names appear in that section?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, those are the names of my colleagues who stood in for me while I was absent, while I took my days off from driving.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And would I be right in saying that even on some days when these people were driving, you would be the one filling out the other page with the locations that the vehicle travelled to? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Can we move to the next page, please? Now, if we look at this page, first I'd like you to go towards, to the last column, where it says the user, and can you confirm that usually, or according to the book, it would have been the responsibility of the user to sign in this column? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: But it was a regular practice that the users did not sign in that column, which then was empty at the end of the month; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for the most part.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And when that was the case at the end of the month, if there was empty spaces in the user column, it would be a regular practice for Drago Nikolic, because he was the main user, to sign in every box, to ensure that the record was complete; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And would I be right in saying that even though a particular column might have the signature of Drago Nikolic, it doesn't necessarily mean that he was the one who used that vehicle on that day? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I'd like to go just to page 4, which is an identical page but for the second part of the month. I'd like to draw your attention, Mr. Bircakovic, to the 17th of July. And if we can zoom in to that date, I see in that column Kravica. Now, what I'd like to know is whether it was you that drove to Kravica on that day and whether you recall driving to Kravica on that day.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And can you explain where you went on that day and why?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, on that day, we went to attend a colleague's funeral. That colleague was killed during the breakout from Srebrenica towards Nezuk at Baljkovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And would I be right saying that this colleague is Dusan Nikolic, who was the first cousin of Drago Nikolic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And Drago Nikolic was with you when you travelled to Kravica?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. I think the entire military police detail was there. We went there in a van.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, you yourself, Mr. Bircakovic, are not aware -- you're not aware of any killings or any crimes that were committed in Kravica or the Kravica warehouse, are you?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, do you know today that something happened in Kravica warehouse?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I do. The stories started after a while.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: But at the time, you did not know; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to move to a different area. Can you confirm that Drago Nikolic did not have either a call sign or a VHF radio in the vehicle that you were using with him?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He did not have a Motorola. I don't think he ever had a Motorola in his car.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So if somebody wanted to convey a message to Drago Nikolic, one would have to go and see him personally; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, either that or they could call him on the phone at his place, or if he was at one single location.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So let's take, for example, for the few minutes or the little time he was in Orahovac, one would have to go there to see him, right, to speak to him?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I move to a different area, and that is an individual, a question was asked of you yesterday by the Prosecution, called Gojko Simic. You said that you know Gojko Simic and that you saw him in Orahovac. What I'd like to know is, because in this interview, you said that you heard that he was there but that you did not see him. What is it today? Did you see him or did you hear that he was in Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I saw him. I was standing on the road, and I saw him walking towards the front line. He was on his way back from the holiday that he had had, and he went towards the line, using the same road to Parlog and Baljkovica where they had their line.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, with respect to Gojko Simic, would I be right in saying that you heard that his son was going to the army and also that he was killed a few days after the events in Orahovac? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. His son had a sendoff before that, and when there was this break through towards Baljkovica, he got killed in the Baljkovica company.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to move to a different area, and I have a few miscellaneous questions to end my cross-examination, the first one being: Something was asked of you during your interview concerning the removal of bodies later on in time, far after the events in Orahovac. Can you confirm what you stated in the interview, that you know nothing about these events or what happened concerning the removal of bodies later on?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know about that. I only know that I took Trbic to Petkovci, that he got out of the car, he looked around, he stayed there maybe a minute or so, and then we returned. At the time, nothing was done with regard to the removal. I don't know anything about that. And that's what I stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And do you know whether this visit of Trbic had any relationship with the removal of bodies or it's just a place that you went and you recall the time and the place and nothing more?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was just that time and that place. We just went there. Nothing else. Just went to that place at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So you don't know whether this is related in fact to the removal of bodies; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It did not have anything to do with the removal of bodies. I'm sure of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, one question I just forgot concerning your driving of Drago Nikolic. Can you confirm that on the 16th of July, you drove Drago Nikolic to meet the family of Dusan Nikolic and then to the hospital, and that was on the 16th of July? Do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. We all went, not only Drago. Maybe 10 or so people were involved in the burial and the preparations. We went to his family up there. We went to their apartment. This is what we did. I believe that we spent the entire day in that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: My next question has to do with something you mentioned to the investigator assigned to a Defence team of Drago Nikolic, and Mr. President, if I can move in private session, just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Certainly. Let's move into private session for a short while.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I was going to ask you more questions, but I will leave it just one last question. You met with the Prosecution this weekend, and there was one of your answer that really drew our curiosity. And I'd like to read you this answer and then maybe ask you a question with respect to this answer. In the notes that we've been -- now, these are the notes that were prepared by the Prosecution when you met with them, and one of the things you mentioned is, and I quote, "He recalled driving away from the Orahovac school area in the course of 14 July 1995, to Zvornik and to Karakaj. He stated that he could have left the area if there had been an order but cannot recall who ordered this or why he went to Zvornik and Karakaj." My first question is: This -- well, do you recall that you mentioned this to the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So my understanding of this paragraph is that this happened during the day which you spent in Orahovac. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And is it possible that it is Drago Nikolic that you took to Zvornik and Karakaj on the 14th of July?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: But you don't recall who it is that you took away from Orahovac, if you took somebody away from Orahovac on that day?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe one of the people who were there. I don't know. I can't remember. In any case, I did go there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And I'd like to know if you -- just a few questions concerning the 13th of July. I'd like you to try to remember whether you recall on the 13th of July following a UNHCR convoy that drove to Bratunac along with Trbic. Is that something that you recall happening on the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There is something there, but I can't remember exactly what it was. Those convoys carrying humanitarian aid were escorted. That's true. I personally escorted such convoys on many occasions, up to Bratunac and back.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And my last question, Mr. Bircakovic, is: Can you confirm that the Zvornik Brigade did not have, in its fleet of vehicles, an Opel Kadet Suza, the coupe type, can you confirm this?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't think so. There were Peugeot vehicles, there was an Opel Rekord, the Opel Rekord that we were talking about. It had a Volkswagen Passat. I can't confirm that there was a Suza, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: With your leave, Mr. President, I just want to verify that I didn't forget any questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: One last question, Mr. Bircakovic, and I'm done. Do you recall whether anyone brought you some food while you were in Orahovac on the 14th of July? And I say you. It could have been you and the other people who were there on that day.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about other men. I believe that on the way to Zvornik and Karakaj, I had lunch on the way there or something to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And do you recall anyone taking food to the -- to those who were in Orahovac on the 14th of July?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that. I know that there was water and that they got water.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Bircakovic. I have no further questions. Thank you. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Bourgon. It's the Borovcanin Defence team's turn now. Mr. Stojanovic, how much time do you think you require?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, up to half an hour. If you recall, yesterday we said that we might not have any questions, bearing in mind that the civilian police was not mentioned during the examination-in-chief. But in paragraph 30, count 30, Ljubomir Borovcanin is not charged with the events in Orahovac. We would kindly allow Your Honour's permission to clarify some things with this regard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Go ahead. And may I ask -- get a confirmation from the Gvero and the Miletic Defence teams that they are not cross-examining this witness? Madam Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President, we won't have any questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And Mr. Haynes?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Correct on behalf of Gvero, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: 15 to 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So this witness has to return tomorrow. Go ahead, Mr. Stojanovic, you may start now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Bircakovic. Today, to my colleague's questions, you mentioned your contacts which you had with the civilian police when you escorted the convoy. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You say that on the bus where you were, on the road from Divic to Orahovac, there were four policemen, do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Four or five maybe.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to read to you one part of your interview with the investigators. For identification, this is in the version that contains both B/C/S and English, page 47 and part of page 48. It says here, Mr. Bircakovic, to the investigator's question, "Tell me once again who escorted these men, can you describe the escorts?" Your answer was this: "They wore civilian -- I mean civilian police. I mean civilian clothes. They didn't wear camouflage uniforms. They wore uniforms of the civilian police. There were four or five of them on the bus, four or five policemen." Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And you can still confirm that as you sit here today?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Allow me then to ask for another clarification. What did you mean by civilian police uniforms that were not camouflage uniforms? Were those blue overalls or blue two-piece uniforms?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were blue uniforms, such as were worn by the then-police that moved around the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: They didn't wear overalls?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Their -- they might have been overalls. In any case, they were civilian police, as far as that is concerned. Maybe they were blue uniforms of the civilian police, that the civilian policemen wore.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Did they consist of two pieces or just one piece?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think just one piece. Those were overalls. I'm not sure. I'm not sure. But I know that --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The bus that you got on, it was the first to arrive at Vidikovac; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Today, you have told us that you did not see any other vehicle in front of you.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You've also told us that you did not see an APC, a UN APC in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember having seen it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to show you another statement provided by a witness that we heard, who was protected. He was one of the survivors from Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Mr. Stojanovic. Yes, Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Again, Your Honours, there is no reason for this background to load up the question with, This is of a witness who testified here, et cetera. He can easily read the passage or give the proposition and say, do you agree with that, do you not agree with that, is that true, is that not true, or what do you have to say about that statement?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic? Now you've said it in any case, but I would suggest that you proceed along the lines indicated by Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. This is what I will do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: This is what I want to ask you. It says in this statement, "When we arrived at the road towards Josanica, there is a stone quarry there. From there we took off for Divic. As we left the tunnel, somebody saw an APC by the hotel Vidikovac. It was some 800 metres away from us. We continued our journey. We passed through Divic. And we arrived in Zvornik. "When we arrived at Karakaj, the lorries and the buses turned off to the left, in the direction of Tuzla," and later on it says,"When we arrived in front of the school, we realised that this was really a UN APC, but it had been captured by the Serbs." My question is this: Does this jog your memory? Can you remember that there was an APC with UN markings on it?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, this wasn't the case. I can't remember that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: We had an occasion to hear another testimony by the man who conducted that UN vehicle and who was leading the convoy. He drove that UN vehicle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I am at a loss. We have just agreed that this is not the procedure that you should be following barely two minutes ago and now you resort to the same procedure that I had suggested you should abandon. You don't need to tell the witness who may have said this or that. I mean, just put the proposition to the witness and ask him whether he agrees with it or not, without referring to any particular witness or to any particular evidence. He doesn't even need to know whether this has been testified or not. I'm sorry if I'm abrupt but --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Thank you for your assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, my question is this: Would you agree, faced with the things that I'm telling you, that there was an APC in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If there was, I don't remember. That may well have been the case. I cannot guarantee that it wasn't. But I don't remember. If I remembered, why wouldn't I say that there was? There is nothing for me to gain by not saying that I remember. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On that day, do you remember having seen, in front of your bus, on the bus where you were, a Golf with civilian police markings?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me if I told you that when this convoy was being organised, and according to some information it left Bratunac on the 14th of July, in every bus there was a soldier of the VRS providing security for the convoy and the bus of the convoy that was moving in the direction of Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, before you answer, Mr. Bircakovic. Yes, Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. It arises from this question that the witness is supposed to talk about the organisation of this convoy in Bratunac, and I don't think that the witness ever mentioned having been in Bratunac when the convoy was being organised, so I don't think this is an appropriate question for this witness put in this way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: According to the logbook, he did go to Bratunac on one or two occasions but that may be beside the point. Yes, Mr. Stojanovic, after having heard Mr. Zivanovic, do you wish to proceed with your question or do you wish to pass to the next one?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will rephrase the question. I don't have any problem with that. I'm trying to avoid quoting any more statements and testimonies by various witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: My question, therefore, is this: Would it jog your memory if I told you that there is a possibility that on every one of those buses, and you were on the first one of them, that there was a VRS soldier providing security for the buses?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD BIRCAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether there was or whether there wasn't. I know that there were four or five civilian policemen who escorted those buses. Whether the soldiers were there or not, I don't know. I only know that not only in my bus but in every other bus, there were four or five men who had arrived on the buses, which means that every bus had its security. Those men were on the buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Allow me to face you with P00220. This is a Prosecutor's exhibit. This is the logbook of the duty officer of the Bratunac Brigade. Let us look at the ERN 0663926, page 17 in e-court, the English version. Page 14 in e-court, of the English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honour, just for clarity of the record, the transcript has down duty officer log, and what this exhibit is titled, and it's entitled on the list given to us by my friends is that this is the Bratunac Brigade military police daily log, so for the record, that's what we've got here is an MP log, not a duty officer notebook.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you for pointing that out. We've got -- we haven't got more time. It's just a few seconds before 7.00. So I suggest that you -- we adjourn now and we proceed tomorrow. The sitting tomorrow starts at 2.15 in the afternoon. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
